ops.entry: WHEN checking whether a member folded your instructions in DO grep one distinctive token of the fact each names — the cited line, the identifier — never your own wording or a multi-word phrase: members rephrase and line wraps split phrases, so either grep reports absent what is there.
ops.why: Absorbs G-11 (line-wrapped phrase grep) into P-14 (phrasing grep): same check, same failure, one rule; no longer than the longer input. Frees a Gotchas slot.

ops.entry: WHEN you characterize a behaviour delta in a signature question DO test the claim on a data-carrying instance of the shape, not only the minimal example — a delta reasoned from an empty instance reads as harmless, and the signer inherits the overgeneralization as a ruling.
ops.why: My plan digest called the malformed-v2 writer delta stderr-only from a rowless example; the signoff repeated it as bytes-identical, and the c0 ruling had to correct it after row-carrying envelopes were shown to lose live rows. Old G-11 is absorbed into P-14.

originals.original: WHEN checking whether a member folded your instructions in DO grep for the fact each names — the cited line, the identifier — never your own wording. A member writes its own prose but carries the anchor verbatim, so a phrasing-grep reports absent what is there.

WHEN grepping for an anchor phrase inside a YAML block scalar or hard-wrapped prose DO search one distinctive token rather than the multi-word phrase — a line wrap splits the phrase across two physical lines, and grep then reports ABSENT what is present and correctly written.
